description: Design a 4-bit down counter that counts down from a specified value to 0, then resets to the specified value. The counter should decrement on each clock cycle and have an active-low reset signal. The counter will also have a load signal to set the counter to a new initial value.
code:
module down_counter (
    input clk,
    input rst_n, // active low reset
    input load,
    input [3:0] init_value,
    output reg [3:0] count
);

always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        count <= 4'b0000; // reset to 0
    end else if (load) begin
        count <= init_value; // load new value
    end else if (count > 0) begin
        count <= count - 1; // count down
    end
end

endmodule

description: Design a 32-bit serializer that takes 32 parallel input bits and serializes them into a single output bitstream. The serializer should have a clock input to shift out one bit at each clock cycle. The output should be valid for one clock cycle after the corresponding input bit is received. The input should be loaded with a 32-bit value when a load signal is asserted.
code:
module serializer(
    input clk,
    input load,
    input [31:0] data_in,
    output reg serial_out
);
    reg [31:0] shift_reg;
    reg [4:0] bit_count; // 5 bits to count from 0 to 31

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (load) begin
            shift_reg <= data_in; // Load data into shift register
            bit_count <= 0; // Reset bit counter
        end else if (bit_count < 32) begin
            serial_out <= shift_reg[31]; // Output the MSB
            shift_reg <= shift_reg << 1; // Shift left
            bit_count <= bit_count + 1; // Increment bit count
        end else begin
            serial_out <= 0; // No more output after 32 bits
        end
    end
endmodule

module viterbi_decoder (

    input rst,
    input bit_in,
    output reg [1:0] decoded_out
);
    reg state; // current state

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin

            state <= 0;
            decoded_out <= 2'b00;
        end else begin
            // State transition based on input
            case (state)
                0: begin
                    if (bit_in == 0) begin
                        decoded_out <= 2'b00; // output for state 0, input 0
                        state <= 0; // stay in state 0
                    end else begin
                        decoded_out <= 2'b01; // output for state 0, input 1
                        state <= 1; // transition to state 1
                    end

                        decoded_out <= 2'b10; // output for state 1, input 0
                        state <= 0; // transition to state 0

                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description:
Design an 8-bit ALU that can perform the following operations based on a 3-bit control input:
- 000: Addition
- 001: Subtraction
- 010: Bitwise AND
- 011: Bitwise OR
- 100: Bitwise XOR
- 101: Comparison (output 1 if A > B, 0 otherwise)
The ALU should take two 8-bit inputs A and B and produce an 8-bit output Z. Additionally, the comparison will output a single bit result in the MSB of Z, while the rest of the bits of Z will be set to 0 for the comparison operation.
code:
module ALU (
    input [7:0] A,
    input [7:0] B,
    input [2:0] control,
    output reg [7:0] Z
);

always @(*) begin
    case (control)
        3'b000: Z = A + B;            // Addition
        3'b001: Z = A - B;            // Subtraction
        3'b010: Z = A & B;            // Bitwise AND
        3'b011: Z = A | B;            // Bitwise OR
        3'b100: Z = A ^ B;            // Bitwise XOR
        3'b101: Z = (A > B) ? 8'b00000001 : 8'b00000000; // Comparison
        default: Z = 8'b00000000;     // Default case
    endcase
end

endmodule

- A clock input to increment the timer value.
- A watchdog timeout signal that indicates an error if the timer exceeds a predefined value.
- A signal to indicate that the watchdog timer has been reset.

The timer should count up to a specified limit (e.g., 8 clock cycles) and then trigger the timeout signal if it reaches that limit without being reset.
code:
module watchdog_timer (
    input clk,
    input reset_n,
    output reg timeout,
    output reg reset_indicator
);
    parameter TIMEOUT_LIMIT = 8; // Timeout limit
    reg [2:0] counter; // 3-bit counter to count up to 8

    always @(posedge clk or negedge reset_n) begin
        if (!reset_n) begin
            counter <= 3'b000;
            timeout <= 1'b0;
            reset_indicator <= 1'b1; // Indicate reset
        end else begin
            if (counter < TIMEOUT_LIMIT) begin
                counter <= counter + 1;
                timeout <= 1'b0; // No timeout yet
                reset_indicator <= 1'b0; // Reset indicator off
            end else begin
                timeout <= 1'b1; // Timeout occurred
                reset_indicator <= 1'b0; // Reset indicator off
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a non-restoring divider in Verilog that performs integer division of two 4-bit numbers. The output should be a 4-bit quotient and a 4-bit remainder. The inputs are the dividend and divisor, and the division operation should be performed based on the non-restoring division algorithm.
code:
module non_restoring_divider (
    input [3:0] dividend,
    input [3:0] divisor,
    output reg [3:0] quotient,
    output reg [3:0] remainder
);
    reg [4:0] r; // Remainder and the bit to be shifted in
    reg [4:0] d; // Divisor
    
    integer i;

    always @(*) begin
        r = {1'b0, dividend}; // Initialize remainder
        d = {1'b0, divisor}; // Initialize divisor
        quotient = 4'b0; // Initialize quotient

        for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
            r = r << 1; // Shift left
            r[0] = dividend[3 - i]; // Bring in next bit of dividend
            r = r - d; // Subtract divisor
            if (r[4] == 1) begin
                r = r + d; // If negative, restore
                quotient[i] = 0; // Set quotient bit to 0
            end else begin
                quotient[i] = 1; // Set quotient bit to 1
            end
        end
        remainder = r[3:0]; // Final remainder
    end
endmodule

    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [2:0] req,
    output reg [2:0] grant
);
    reg [2:0] last_granted;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            grant <= 3'b000;
            last_granted <= 3'b000;
        end else begin
            if (req[2]) begin
                grant <= 3'b100; // Grant req[2]
                last_granted <= 3'b100;
            end else if (req[1]) begin
                grant <= 3'b010; // Grant req[1]

    input [7:0] data_in,
    output reg tx,
    output reg ready
);

            bit_index <= 0;
            shift_reg <= {1'b1, data_in, 1'b0}; // Prepare shift register (start bit = 0, stop bit = 1)

            tx <= shift_reg[0]; // Transmit the current bit
            shift_reg <= {1'b1, shift_reg[9:1]}; // Shift right
            bit_index <= bit_index + 1;

            if (bit_index == 10) begin

        end

    end
endmodule

    input clk,

    input start,
    input stop,

    output reg done,
    output reg scl,
    output reg sda

    reg [7:0] data;
    reg [2:0] bit_index;

               START = 1,
               SEND = 2,
               STOP = 3;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            scl <= 1;
            sda <= 1;
            done <= 0;
            bit_index <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    done <= 0;
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= START;
                        sda <= 0; // Send start condition
                    end

                START: begin
                    scl <= 0; // Start clock
                    state <= SEND;
                    data <= data_in; // Load data to be sent
                    bit_index <= 0;
                end
                SEND: begin
                    if (bit_index < 8) begin
                        scl <= 0; // Prepare to send bit
                        sda <= data[7 - bit_index]; // Send MSB first
                        scl <= 1; // Clock high for data
                        bit_index <= bit_index + 1;
                    end else begin
                        state <= STOP; // All bits sent
                    end
                end
                STOP: begin
                    scl <= 0; // Prepare to send stop
                    sda <= 0; // Pull SDA low
                    scl <= 1; // Clock high
                    sda <= 1; // Release SDA
                    done <= 1; // Transmission done

                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

            done <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        queue[tail] <= data_in; // Enqueue the starting node
                        tail <= tail + 1;
                        state <= DEQUEUE; // Move to Dequeue state
                    end
                end
                
                DEQUEUE: begin
                    if (head < tail) begin
                        data_out <= queue[head]; // Output current node
                        head <= head + 1; // Move head pointer
                        state <= OUTPUT; // Move to Output state
                    end else begin
                        done <= 1; // Finished traversal
                        state <= IDLE; // Go back to IDLE
                    end
                end
                
                OUTPUT: begin
                    // Wait for the next clock cycle to dequeue again
                    state <= DEQUEUE;
                end
                
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

Design an I2C controller that initiates a start condition, sends a byte of data, and then sends a stop condition. The controller should have inputs for the clock signal (clk), reset (rst), data input (data_in), and control signals (start, stop). The output should be the I2C data line (sda) and clock line (scl). Assume that the data is sent on the rising edge of the clock.
code:
module I2C_Controller(
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire start,
    input wire stop,
    input wire [7:0] data_in,
    output reg sda,
    output reg scl
);
    reg [3:0] state;
    reg [7:0] data;
    reg [2:0] bit_index;

    localparam IDLE = 4'b0000,
               START = 4'b0001,
               SEND = 4'b0010,
               STOP = 4'b0011;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            sda <= 1; // SDA high when idle
            scl <= 1; // SCL high when idle
            bit_index <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= START;
                        sda <= 0; // Start condition
                    end
                end
                START: begin
                    scl <= 0; // Prepare to send
                    data <= data_in; // Load data to send
                    state <= SEND;
                end
                SEND: begin
                    if (bit_index < 8) begin
                        sda <= data[7 - bit_index]; // Send MSB first
                        scl <= 1; // Clock high
                        bit_index <= bit_index + 1;
                    end else begin
                        state <= STOP; // All bits sent
                        bit_index <= 0;
                    end
                end
                STOP: begin
                    scl <= 0; // Prepare for stop
                    sda <= 1; // Stop condition
                    state <= IDLE; // Go back to idle
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

);

            done <= 0;
        end else if (start) begin
            byte_count <= 0;
            done <= 0;
        end else if (byte_count < 4'b1111) begin
            if (rw) begin // Write operation

            end else begin // Read operation
                temp_data <= memory[addr + byte_count]; // Read data from memory
            end
            byte_count <= byte_count + 1;
        end else begin
            done <= 1; // Indicate transfer is complete
        end
    end

endmodule

    input signed [3:0] B,  // Multiplier
    output reg signed [7:0] P  // Product
);
    reg [4:0] M;  // Extended multiplicand
    reg [4:0] Q;  // Extended multiplier
    reg Q_1;      // Previous bit of Q
    integer i;

    initial begin
        P = 0;
        M = {1'b0, A};  // Extend A
        Q = {1'b0, B};  // Extend B
        Q_1 = 0;        // Initialize Q_1 to 0
    end

    always @(*) begin
        // Reset product
        P = 0;
        // Booth's algorithm
        for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
            case ({Q[0], Q_1})
                2'b01: P = P + M;     // Add M to P
                2'b10: P = P - M;     // Subtract M from P
            endcase
            // Arithmetic right shift
            {P[7], P} = {P[7], P} >> 1;  // Shift P
            {Q, Q_1} = {Q, Q_1} >> 1;    // Shift Q and Q_1
            Q[4] = Q[3];                 // Preserve the sign bit
        end
        P = P + {A[3], A[3], A[3], A[3], A};  // Adjust for signed multiplication
    end
endmodule

            vco_freq <= 0;

    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [7:0] dividend,
    input [7:0] divisor,
    output reg [7:0] quotient,
    output reg [7:0] remainder,
    output reg done

    reg [7:0] B; // 8-bit register for the divisor
    reg [3:0] count; // Counter for bit shifts
    reg state; // State to indicate when division is done

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            quotient <= 0;
            remainder <= 0;
            A <= 0;
            B <= 0;
            count <= 0;
            done <= 0;
            state <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (!state) begin
                // Load values and prepare for division
                A <= {8'b0, dividend}; // Load dividend into lower half
                B <= divisor; // Load divisor
                count <= 8; // Set count to the number of bits
                state <= 1; // Move to division state
            end else if (count > 0) begin
                // Shift A left
                A <= {A[14:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
                // Subtract B from A
                if (A[15:8] >= B) begin
                    A[15:8] <= A[15:8] - B; // Perform subtraction
                    quotient <= {quotient[6:0], 1'b1}; // Set quotient bit
                end else begin
                    quotient <= {quotient[6:0], 1'b0}; // Clear quotient bit
                end
                count <= count - 1; // Decrement count
            end else begin
                // Division complete
                remainder <= A[15:8]; // Set remainder
                done <= 1; // Indicate done
                state <= 0; // Reset state for next operation
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

module uart_tx (
    input clk,            // Clock input
    input reset,          // Reset signal
    input [7:0] data_in,  // 8-bit data input
    input start,          // Start transmission signal
    input parity_enable,   // Enable parity bit
    output reg tx,        // Serial transmit output
    output reg busy       // Indicates busy status
);
    parameter BAUD_RATE = 9600;  // Baud rate for the transmission
    parameter CLOCK_FREQ = 50000000; // Clock frequency
    localparam CLKS_PER_BIT = CLOCK_FREQ / BAUD_RATE;

    reg [3:0] state;            // State for FSM
    reg [7:0] shift_reg;        // Shift register for data
    reg [15:0] clk_count;       // Clock divider counter
    reg parity_bit;             // Calculated parity bit

    localparam IDLE = 0, START = 1, DATA = 2, PARITY = 3, STOP = 4;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            tx <= 1;             // Idle state is high
            busy <= 0;
            state <= IDLE;
            clk_count <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start && !busy) begin
                        busy <= 1;
                        clk_count <= 0;
                        shift_reg <= data_in;
                        parity_bit <= ^data_in; // Calculate parity
                        state <= START;
                    end
                end
                START: begin
                    if (clk_count < CLKS_PER_BIT - 1) begin
                        clk_count <= clk_count + 1;
                    end else begin
                        clk_count <= 0;
                        tx <= 0; // Start bit
                        state <= DATA;
                    end
                end
                DATA: begin
                    if (clk_count < CLKS_PER_BIT - 1) begin
                        clk_count <= clk_count + 1;
                    end else begin
                        clk_count <= 0;
                        tx <= shift_reg[0]; // Send each data bit
                        shift_reg <= {1'b0, shift_reg[7:1]}; // Shift right
                        if (shift_reg == 8'b0) begin
                            if (parity_enable) begin
                                state <= PARITY;
                            end else begin
                                state <= STOP;
                            end
                        end
                    end
                end
                PARITY: begin
                    if (clk_count < CLKS_PER_BIT - 1) begin
                        clk_count <= clk_count + 1;
                    end else begin
                        clk_count <= 0;
                        tx <= parity_bit; // Send parity bit
                        state <= STOP;
                    end
                end
                STOP: begin
                    if (clk_count < CLKS_PER_BIT - 1) begin
                        clk_count <= clk_count + 1;
                    end else begin
                        clk_count <= 0;
                        tx <= 1; // Stop bit
                        busy <= 0; // Transmission done
                        state <= IDLE;
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

module brent_kung_adder #(parameter N = 8) (
    input [N-1:0] A,
    input [N-1:0] B,
    output [N-1:0] S,
    output Cout
);
    wire [N:0] C; // Carry wires
    wire [N-1:0] P, G; // Propagate and Generate

    assign P = A ^ B; // Propagate
    assign G = A & B; // Generate

    // Carry computation using Brent-Kung logic
    assign C[0] = 0; // No carry-in for the first stage
    genvar i;
    generate
        for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin : carry_gen
            assign C[i+1] = G[i] | (P[i] & C[i]); // Carry-out

    endgenerate

    // Sum computation
    assign S = P ^ C[N-1:N-1-N]; // Sum outputs
    assign Cout = C[N]; // Final carry-out

endmodule

module cache_lru (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [7:0] addr,
    input [7:0] data,
    input we,          // write enable
    output reg hit     // cache hit indicator
);
    reg [7:0] cache_data[3:0][1:0]; // 4 sets, 2 lines per set
    reg [1:0] lru[3:0];              // 2-bit LRU counter for each set (0: line 0 is LRU, 1: line 1 is LRU)
    wire [1:0] set_index;
    wire [7:0] tag;

    assign set_index = addr[3:2]; // 2 bits for set index
    assign tag = addr[7:4];       // 4 bits for tag

    integer i;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            // Reset cache
            for (i = 0; i < 4; i = i + 1) begin
                cache_data[i][0] = 8'b0;
                cache_data[i][1] = 8'b0;
                lru[i] = 2'b00; // Initialize LRU
            end
            hit <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (we) begin // Write operation
                // Check for LRU line to replace
                if (lru[set_index] == 2'b00) begin
                    cache_data[set_index][0] <= data;
                    lru[set_index] <= 2'b01; // Update LRU
                end else begin
                    cache_data[set_index][1] <= data;
                    lru[set_index] <= 2'b00; // Update LRU
                end
                hit <= 0;
            end else begin // Read operation
                if (cache_data[set_index][0][7:4] == tag) begin
                    hit <= 1; // Hit in line 0
                    lru[set_index] <= 2'b01; // Update LRU
                end else if (cache_data[set_index][1][7:4] == tag) begin
                    hit <= 1; // Hit in line 1
                    lru[set_index] <= 2'b00; // Update LRU
                end else begin
                    hit <= 0; // Miss

Design a simple Direct Memory Access (DMA) controller that manages data transfer between memory and a peripheral device. The DMA controller should be able to start a transfer, monitor the progress of the transfer, and signal when the transfer is complete. The controller should take in a start signal, a read/write control signal, a data bus, and an address bus, and output a done signal when the transfer is complete.

module dma_controller(
    input clk,
    input reset,
    input start,
    input rw, // 0 for read, 1 for write
    input [7:0] data_in, // Data from memory or peripheral
    output reg [7:0] data_out, // Data to memory or peripheral
    output reg done
);

               READ = 3'b001,
               WRITE = 3'b010,
               DONE = 3'b011;

        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
            done <= 0;
            data_out <= 0;
            address <= 0;
        end else begin

                        state <= rw ? WRITE : READ;
                        done <= 0;
                    end

                    data_out <= data_in; // Read data
                    state <= DONE;
                end
                WRITE: begin
                    // Write data logic (to memory or peripheral)

Design a simple memory allocator that can allocate and free memory blocks. The memory manager will have the following inputs:
- `request`: a request signal to allocate or free memory
- `size`: the size of the memory block to allocate or free
- `free`: a signal to indicate if the operation is a free operation (1 for free, 0 for allocate)

The output will be an `allocated` signal indicating whether the allocation was successful or not. The memory manager should keep track of allocated memory and ensure that it does not allocate more than the available memory.
code:

    input clk,
    input reset,
    input request,
    input [3:0] size,
    input free, // 1 for free, 0 for allocate
    output reg allocated
);

    reg [3:0] allocated_memory = 0; // Currently allocated memory

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            allocated_memory <= 0;
            allocated <= 0;
        end else begin
            if (request) begin
                if (~free) begin // Allocate memory
                    if (allocated_memory + size <= total_memory) begin
                        allocated_memory <= allocated_memory + size;
                        allocated <= 1; // Allocation successful
                    end else begin
                        allocated <= 0; // Not enough memory
                    end

                    if (allocated_memory >= size) begin
                        allocated_memory <= allocated_memory - size;

                        allocated <= 0; // Not enough memory to free

                end
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 32-bit CRC (Cyclic Redundancy Check) generator that takes a 32-bit input and a 1-bit enable signal. When enabled, the module should compute the CRC for the input data according to a polynomial, and output the resulting 32-bit CRC value. The CRC should be updated on every clock cycle. The module should also have a reset signal that initializes the CRC value to zero.
code:
module crc32_generator(
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire enable,
    input wire [31:0] data_in,
    output reg [31:0] crc_out
);
    reg [31:0] crc;
    parameter POLYNOMIAL = 32'h04C11DB7; // Example polynomial

    integer i;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            crc <= 32'b0;
        end else if (enable) begin
            crc = crc ^ data_in; // Initial XOR with input data
            for (i = 0; i < 32; i = i + 1) begin
                if (crc[31] == 1'b1) begin
                    crc = (crc << 1) ^ POLYNOMIAL;
                end else begin
                    crc = crc << 1;
                end
            end
        end
    end

    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (enable) begin
            crc_out <= crc;
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a carrier frequency recovery circuit using a phase-locked loop (PLL) in Verilog. The PLL should consist of a phase detector, a low-pass filter, and a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO). The input to the PLL is a noisy signal containing a carrier frequency, and the output should be a clean clock signal that is synchronized with the carrier frequency.
code:
module pll (
    input wire clk_in,       // The noisy input signal
    input wire reset,        // Reset signal
    output reg clk_out       // The recovered clock output
);

reg [3:0] phase_error;      // Phase error signal
reg [3:0] filter_output;     // Filter output 
reg [3:0] vco_output;        // Output from the VCO
reg [3:0] vco_count;         // VCO count

// Phase detector logic
always @(posedge clk_in or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        phase_error <= 0;
    end else begin
        // Simple phase detection logic
        phase_error <= phase_error + (clk_in ? 1 : -1);
    end
end

// Low pass filter logic
always @(posedge clk_in or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        filter_output <= 0;
    end else begin
        filter_output <= (filter_output + phase_error) >> 1; // Simple averaging
    end
end

// Voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) logic
always @(posedge clk_in or posedge reset) begin
    if (reset) begin
        vco_count <= 0;
        clk_out <= 0;
    end else begin
        vco_count <= vco_count + filter_output;   // Adjust frequency based on filter output
        if (vco_count >= 4) begin
            clk_out <= ~clk_out;                  // Toggle output on reaching threshold
            vco_count <= 0;                       // Reset count
        end
    end
end

endmodule

Design a Kogge-Stone adder for 4-bit inputs. The Kogge-Stone adder should compute the sum and carry out for two 4-bit binary numbers.
code:
module kogge_stone_adder (
    input [3:0] A,
    input [3:0] B,
    output [3:0] S,
    output Cout
);
    wire [3:0] P; // Generate
    wire [3:0] G; // Propagate
    wire [3:0] C; // Carry

    assign P = A ^ B; // Propagate
    assign G = A & B; // Generate

    assign C[0] = G[0]; // First carry
    assign C[1] = G[1] | (P[1] & C[0]);
    assign C[2] = G[2] | (P[2] & C[1]);
    assign C[3] = G[3] | (P[3] & C[2]);

    assign S = P ^ C; // Sum
    assign Cout = C[3]; // Carry out

endmodule
